facts.fact: The Hollow Moon route-song, taught to Kunal, runs: 'Fan on the left hand, cold ridge on the right, count three hundred where the snow goes blue, and a hundred more to light.' It is eight paces short of Ila's measured three hundred and eight.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Kunal steer by song while Ila steers by bearings and paces.

facts.fact: The Hollow Moon's winter line shows only at old waist-high cairns spaced a few hundred paces apart, running north along the bowl's east wall in its shadow, with the watchers' fire a mile and an eighth away on the west lip at about 315 degrees.
facts.why: needed because the beat sets a night crossing past the watchers by cairn-light with dark between.

facts.fact: An avalanche slope of about 38 degrees, wind-loaded from the north-west, lies on the east wall between the third and fourth cairns; its lower third is undercut by a spring-fed summer stream channel (Kunal put a mule through it last July). Ila crosses the middle at stated odds of one in five that it slides.
facts.why: needed because the beat calls for a competence duet on an avalanche slope.

facts.fact: Ila's pencil leads, which snap in cold, are carried by Kunal inside his coat against his chest and handed to her warm one at a time; Ila had mentioned the breaking once to the air on the Stair.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires his specific care to pay off her earlier mention.

facts.fact: Ila did not write the name 'Hollow Moon' when Kunal said it carelessly on the cliff, and writes it only when he repeats it deliberately at night. She also tells him the Taravan archive clerk refused her the Shilak Cairn file (matches F426).
facts.why: needed because the beat has the name trade and his question about who reads her map.

facts.fact: Ila draws the watchers' camp on her sheet (fire, two humps marked 'tents?', an object marked 'unclear') and tells Kunal she has done so.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires her to choose to draw the camp and tell him.

facts.fact: The Hollow Moon's route-keeper cairn at the bowl's north lip (Dhanu calls it 'the door') is toppled, its slab cracked, and three bell marks are scratched on a fallen stone; Kunal identifies the bell as Raghu's mark.
facts.why: needed because the beat ends on the toppled cairn scratched with Raghu's mark.
